subject: spotted salamander
title: This Salamander Has Algae Living Inside Its Own Cells

scenes.text: There's an animal with a backbone that runs partly on sunlight.
Spotted salamander eggs glow green in spring ponds. Scientists noticed it in 1888.
The green is algae, living in the jelly and feeding the embryos oxygen.
In 2010, a researcher looked closer and found the algae inside the embryo's own cells.
No other vertebrate is known to carry photosynthetic algae inside its cells.
A salamander, partly powered by the Sun. It took over 120 years to spot.

description:
Green algae (Oophila) have been known to live in spotted salamander egg masses since 1888. In 2010 Ryan Kerney found the algae inside the cells of the salamander embryos, the first known case of a photosynthetic symbiont inside vertebrate cells (published in PNAS in 2011).
The algae supply oxygen and the embryos give them waste nitrogen.
What other animal do you think could be secretly solar powered?
first_comment: The sea slug Elysia steals chloroplasts too, but it has no backbone. Which would you rather be: solar or sea slug?
